title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
authors: Tong Zheng, Xidong Wu, Zheng Zhang, Zhankui He, Chaoyi Zhang, Benjamin Coleman, Ruoqiao Wei, Di Bai, Haolin Liu, Rui Liu, Xue Wang, Yue Zhuan, Wang-Cheng Kang, Renkai Xiang, Heng Huang, Xinwu Cheng, Yunsong Guo (corresponding: Xidong Wu, Zheng Zhang)
lab: Google, University of Maryland College Park, Google DeepMind, University of Virginia (affiliations as the project README gives them)
date: 14 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version on 3 October 2026)

code.title: zhengkid/Dream-RSI
code.link_label: github.com/zhengkid/Dream-RSI holds only the paper and figures
code.note: No code, traces or discovered programs yet: the README's release plan lists the full codebase, reproduction scripts and discovered programs as "being prepared" (checked 3 October 2026). The repository has a README, a citation file, figure assets and the paper PDF, and no licence

takeaway: Treat an agent's accumulated discovery history as a replay simulator over the search space already explored, so exploration policies can be improved off-policy by "dreaming" against past evaluations instead of paying for new ones; competitive or better solution quality at substantially lower discovery cost across algorithm engineering, mathematical optimisation and GPU kernel engineering.
verdict: Believe the idea: a finished search tree is a free, exact record against which a new exploration policy can be re-scored for how it would have spent the same evaluations, and that plausibly buys the same results for fewer calls. Treat the results as anecdotes: one run per setting with no error bars, a cost count that leaves out the policy-writing agent's own work, ratios that shrink at matched performance (VGG16 2.43× becomes 1.89×, LayerNorm 1.79× becomes 1.19×), and a Lasso headline carried by one dataset of six.

headline.k: Lasso solver discovery with Gemini-3.1-Pro, average held-out runtime 3,587.1 → 2,931.0 ms
headline.d: but faster than fixed exploration on 1 of the 6 datasets; RCV1 is 91% of the average

headline.k: fewer generations on the VGG16 and LayerNorm kernels at "comparable performance"
headline.d: ratios of total budgets; at matched performance 1.89× and 1.19×

headline.k: higher speed on the ConvDiv and ConvMax kernels at a similar budget
headline.d: one run each; ConvMax's gain is one jump in the last round

resources.n: the method in prose, the result tables, and an animated one-lap demo whose numbers the page itself labels illustrative; it is also the only place that says what the dagger in the Lasso table means ("our reproduction").

resources.t: Structured Scaling of AI Discovery Across Diverse Scientific Domains (SimpleTES)
resources.by: Ye et al., arXiv 2604.19341 (v2, 27 July 2026; Dream-RSI cites it under its earlier title, "Evaluation-driven scaling for scientific discovery")
resources.n: the strongest baseline and the source of the Lasso task, its 17 search instances and the 51,200-generation budget (C = 32 trajectories × L = 100 steps × K = 16 samples); its Supplementary Table 16 is where Dream-RSI's SimpleTES row comes from.
the online alternative Dream-RSI argues against: evolve the search strategy itself during discovery, paying a real rollout for each strategy tried.

resources.t: AlphaEvolve: a coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
resources.by: Novikov et al., Google DeepMind, arXiv 2506.13131
resources.n: the discovery loop (propose, evaluate, keep the best) with a hand-designed exploration strategy, and the source of the autocorrelation and circle-packing baselines in Table 1.

resources.t: KernelBench: can LLMs write efficient GPU kernels?
resources.n: the benchmark behind the four kernel tasks (VGG16, LayerNorm, ConvDiv, ConvMax): correctness against a PyTorch reference, then speed.
the analogy the paper borrows: train a policy inside a model of the environment instead of the environment. Dream-RSI's "model" is not learned; it is the recorded tree itself.

resources.t: Mastering diverse domains through world models (DreamerV3)
resources.n: the Dreamer line the paper names: learn a dynamics model from experience and improve the policy on imagined trajectories.

for the general picture the paper's Section 2 sketches, including Sutton's Dyna (1990): plan with simulated experience between real steps, and the known risk that a policy exploits the model where the model is wrong.

kb.t: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
kb.n: One of the week's three auto-research papers. Its population converged prematurely and a human had to restore diversity, the opposite failure from a replay simulator that can only reward what the history already covers.

kb.t: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
kb.n: The third of that week's auto-research papers: its memory lives in harness-layer techniques discovered once and reused, where Agora's lives in a shared commit graph and Dream-RSI's in replayable trees.

kb.t: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
kb.n: Recursive self-improvement in the weights (interactions served through a routing harness become a post-training curriculum); Dream-RSI keeps every model fixed and changes only the exploration policy's code. Neither ablates its own loop.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: Another way to change the layer around a fixed agent: write a new harness per task. JIT-Agent trains the writer; Dream-RSI scores rewrites of one policy against old traces.

kb.t: Φ-Bench: Can Large Language Models Engineer the Infrastructure That Powers Them?
kb.n: Kernel and hardware work is where frontier models score worst there (Hardware and Edge 5.4% for the best model), which is one of Dream-RSI's three demonstration domains.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: The score a harness creator could see moved the same way as the held-out score in only 34 of 64 version changes: the same question of whether a self-edit judged on old runs generalises.

kb.t: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
kb.n: Cited by Dream-RSI (Huang et al. 2026b) among self-evolving systems that build environments; there the world is generated, here it is the agent's own history.

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: Another recursive self-improvement loop over the layer around a fixed model, with a regulariser against drift.

topics.n: off-policy evaluation and model-based planning, the ideas the paper borrows.
the orchestration layer around a coding agent, where this paper's change lives.
self-improvement loops that do not touch weights, against those that do.
